questions.question: Which of the following is **not **a style of Temple Architecture in India?
questions.solution:
__**Gothic Style**__ is **not** a style of Temple Architecture in India.

 
• The styles of Temple Architecture in India include Nagara, Vesara, Dravida, Gadag, Kalinga, Maru-Gurjara.
 
• **Nagara** is the **northern style**, **Vesara** is the **mixed** style, and **Dravida** is the **southern style**.
 
• Gothic Style is a European architecture style that exhibits a delicate and intricate aesthetic.
 
• This style can be found in cathedrals and churches.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a metalloid?
questions.solution:
__**Carbon**__ is not a metalloid and is a non-metal.

 
• Metalloids are those elements possessing properties between non-metals and metals.
 
• These are also known as semi-metals.
 
• The elements which are metalloids, in the periodic table are boron, silicon, arsenic, antimony, polonium, and tellurium.
 
• Metalloids are semiconductors.

questions.question: Who captained the Indian cricket team to victory in the 1983 cricket World cup?
questions.solution:
__**Kapil Dev**__ captained the Indian cricket team to victory in **1983 cricket World Cup**.

 
• He was the **first Indian captain** to lift the World Cup on 25th June 1983.
 
• West Indies was defeated by India- by 43 runs.
 
• India batted first and was bowled out for 183 in 54.5 overs.
 
• Roger Binny of the Indian team was the leading wicket-taker.

questions.question: Who implements Model Code of conduct for elections in India?
questions.solution:
__**Election Commission**__ implements the Model Code of conduct for elections in India.

 
• Election Commission is a **permanent body** of India.
 
• Model Code of Conduct is a set of instructions that should be **followed by political parties** contesting elections and candidates in the fray.
 
• It consists of instructions and guidelines on meetings, general conduct, campaigning, etc. during elections.
 
• It remains effective until the completion of the entire process of elections.

questions.question: Who among the following played a major role in the Bardoli Satyagraha?
questions.solution:
__**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**__ played a major role in the **Bardoli Satyagraha**.

 
• The movement, in 1928, was led by him for the farmers of Bardoli against the unfair raising of taxes.
 
• Those who supported the British and paid taxes were socially boycotted.
 
• The revenue was thus reduced by 6.03% and the peasants got back their confiscated lands.
 
• Gandhiji also supported the movement.

questions.question: Which Central Institution monitors and regulates agricultural credit in India?
questions.solution:
Option **1** is correct, i.e. __**NABARD**__.

__
 
• **NABARD**__ monitors and regulates agricultural credit in India.
 
• NABARD stands for National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development.
 
• NABARD refers to the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.
 
• NABARD was formed on the recommendation of the committee formed on 30 March 1979, under the Chairmanship of Shri B. Sivaraman.
 
• It came into existence on 12 July 1982 by transferring the agricultural credit functions of RBI and refinance functions of the then Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation (ARDC).
 
• NABARD today is fully owned by the Government of India.

questions.question: ________ is the change in total utility due to consumption of one additional unit of a commodity.
questions.solution:

• In terms of economics, utility refers to the total satisfaction received from consuming a service or good.
 
• When the supply of goods or services increases, economic utility can decline.

questions.question: Who is the first Indian cricketer to score four centuries in the World Cup?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Which city was recognised as "City of Music" by UNESCO?
questions.solution:
**Varanasi** was recognized as **"City of Music"** by UNESCO in **2015**.

 
• It was chosen in the music category under the 'field of excellence' plan of UNESCO.
 
• The categories under the field of excellence include gastronomy, media arts, design, music, film, craft and folk art, and literature.
 
• The other cities which are a part of 'Cities of Music' include Bologna, Seville, Bogota, Brazzaville, Hamamatsu, Ghent, Mannheim, Hanover, and Glasgow.
 
• Seville and Bologna were the inaugural Cities of Music.

questions.question: Which of the following functional group of carbon does NOT contain oxygen?
questions.solution:
**Halogen** does not contain oxygen.

 
• Halogens such as chlorine and fluorine are oxidizing agents which do not contain oxygen.
 
• **Alcohol** is an organic molecule that is assembled from hydrogen, oxygen, and carbon atoms.
 
• **Aldehydes** are organic compounds in which a carbon atom shares a single bond with hydrogen, double bond with oxygen.
 
• **Ketones** are organic compounds having carbon atom covalently bonded to an oxygen atom.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered fiat money?
questions.solution:
__**Gold**__ is not considered **fiat money.**

 
• **Fiat money** is the currency **issued by the government** which is **not backed by any physical commodity** such as silver or gold.
 
• **Paper currency, coins, and demand drafts** are **fiat money**.
 
• Its value is derived from the relationship between demand and supply and the stability of the issuing government.
 
• It gives central banks of the government greater control over the economy.

questions.question: Phloem is responsible for transport of which substance in plants?
questions.solution:
__**Phloem**__ is responsible for the transport of __**food substances**__ in plants.

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• Phloem

 
 
• It is the complex tissue that acts as a transport system for soluble organic compounds within vascular plants.
 
• It transports the food made in leaves to other parts of plants.
 
• It is made up of living tissue, which uses turgor pressure and energy in the form of ATP to actively transport sugars to the plant organs
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Xylem

 
 
• It is a type of tissue in vascular plants that transports water and some nutrients from the roots to the leaves.
 
• The tissue consists of a variety of specialized, water-conducting cells known as tracheary elements.
 
 
 
• Root hairs
 
 
• These are cylindrical extensions of root epidermal cells.
 
• The primary function is to collect water and mineral nutrients from the soil. It takes the solution up by the roots to the rest of the plant.
 
 
 
• Epiblema
 
 
• Epidermis with root hairs is called epiblema.
 
• It is composed of one layer of compactly arranged parenchymatous cells.
 
• It is usually located between the epidermis and cortex in the root or stem of a plant.
 
• The root hairs and thin-walled epiblema cells absorb water and minerals salts from the soil.

questions.question: Which of the following disease is NOT transmitted through water?
questions.solution:
__**Measles**__ is not transmitted through water.

It is a **viral disease** that spreads through sneezing and coughing.

__Explanation:__

Water-Borne diseases: 

These are conditions caused by pathogenic micro-organisms that are transmitted in water. The disease can spread while bathing, washing or drinking water, or by eating food exposed to infected water and can cause severe, life-threatening diseases. Examples are typhoid fever, cholera and Hepatitis A or E. Other microorganisms induce less dangerous diseases such as diarrhoea. 

__
 
• Cholera: Cholera is a waterborne disease and is diarrhoeal in nature.
 
• Typhoid: It is another disease that gets transmitted by drinking contaminated water that carries ‘Salmonellae Typhi bacteria’.
 
• Diarrhoea: Diarrhoea is one of the most common waterborne diseases that mostly affects children under the age of 5.
 
• Hepatitis A: Another type of waterborne disease is Hepatitis A and it is caused by Hepatitis A virus, which affects the liver.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Dialysis is recommended to a patient having which human organ damaged or not working properly?
questions.solution:
**Dialysis** is recommended to a patient having __**kidney**__ damaged or not working properly.

 
• It is a treatment that removes salt, waste, and extra water from the body and helps control blood pressure.
 
• Kidneys are bean-shaped organs that are responsible for filtering blood in the body.
 
• It helps maintain the right levels of electrolytes, control the body's fluid balance, and removes waste.
 
• However, when it stops functioning normally, that is when dialysis is required.

questions.question: A narrow passage of water connecting two large water bodies like seas and oceans is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e., __Strait.__

__
 
• A narrow passage of water connecting two large water bodies like seas and oceans is called **strait**__.
 
• Example - Strait of Malacca.
 
• A **lagoon** is a water body separated from larger water bodies by a natural barrier.
 
• A narrow strip of land that separates two water bodies and connects two larger landmasses is known as an **isthmus**.
 
• Example - Isthmus of Panama.
 
• A broad inlet or a small water body that is set off from a larger water body where the land curves inward is known as a **bay**.
 
• Example- Bay of Bengal.
